name: com.sitesinthewoods/monitor
title: Sites in the Woods
description: Your team's website monitoring: uptime, incidents, speed, TLS and domain expiry.

tools.name: check_site
tools.description: Check a site once: what search engines and agents find. Reads a domain's robots.txt, homepage, sitemap, 404 page and the files agents look for, scores it A to F, and keeps the report at /check/<domain> (or only at its own address, with private). Needs no key. (POST /check)

domain.description: The site's domain or address: example.com

private.description: Keep the report off the domain's page: it's only at its own address. Default false

tools.name: get_check_report
tools.description: A domain's latest public report, as data. The newest public report for a domain, the same data POST /check answers. Needs no key. (GET /check/{domain}/data.json)

tools.name: start_watching
tools.description: Start watching a site, with no account, key or email. Starts checking a site's homepage now, for someone who has no account yet, and answers a private results link and a claim link for the person the agent works for. Needs no key. (POST /start)

url.description: The site's address or domain: example.com

tools.name: get_start_results
tools.description: An unclaimed site's results. What the results link answers. Needs no key. (GET /start/s/{token})

token.description: The results link's token (sr_…): the end of the `results` link POST /start answered. Private: never post it or send it to another site

tools.name: renew_claim_link
tools.description: A new claim link for your person. Makes a fresh claim link for an unclaimed site, from its results link's token, when you hand it over or your person lost theirs. Needs no key. (POST /start/s/{token}/claim)

token.description: The results link's token (sr_…): the end of the `results` link POST /start answered. Private: never post it or send it to another site

tools.name: forget_results_link
tools.description: Forget a results link. Stops this results link working. Needs no key. (POST /start/s/{token}/forget)

token.description: The results link's token (sr_…): the end of the `results` link POST /start answered. Private: never post it or send it to another site

tools.name: give_feedback
tools.description: Tell us where you got stuck, what answered wrong, or what's missing. A person reads every message. Needs no key. (POST /feedback)

message.description: What happened, in your own words: what you were trying to do, what you called, and what got in the way (at most 2000 characters). Never include a key, a token or a private link

category.description: stuck: something blocked you; wrong: an answer or doc was wrong; missing: something you needed isn't there; praise: something worked well

tool.description: The tool, route or operation it's about (an identifier, like check or POST /start)

severity.description: high: you couldn't finish what your person asked

tools.name: get_status
tools.description: Every one of the team's sites: its status right now, and the open incidents. Call this first, or on a schedule (at most once a minute, as often as the checks run), to see whether anything is down or warning right now. (GET /api/status)

tools.name: list_sites
tools.description: The team's sites: status, homepage uptime over 1, 7 and 30 days, open incidents. Call this to compare sites or report on uptime over the last day, week or month. (GET /api/sites)

domain.description: only the site on this domain (example.com, www.example.com or a URL; matched by host, without www.): an empty list when the team has none

tools.name: get_site
tools.description: One site: its last 7 days (as in the weekly brief), open incidents, domain and TLS expiry. Call this to answer questions about one site. (GET /api/sites/{slug})

tools.name: get_site_insights
tools.description: One site's daily insights: page weight, headers, errors, links, caching and dead ends. Call this when a site is slow or heavy, or to find what to fix. (GET /api/sites/{slug}/insights)

tools.name: list_scans
tools.description: One site's API recovery scans, newest first: state, how each ended, and findings by weight. Call this to see whether a site has been scanned for dead ends, and how the last scan came out. (GET /api/sites/{slug}/scans)

tools.name: get_scan
tools.description: One API recovery scan: what it saw, its findings, the fixes and what changed since the last scan. Call this for a scan's results. (GET /api/sites/{slug}/scans/{id})

tools.name: list_maintenance
tools.description: One site's maintenance windows: on now, scheduled, and the last 30 days. Call this to see whether a site is in a maintenance window (its alerts held, its uptime not counting that time) and when the next one is. (GET /api/sites/{slug}/maintenance)

tools.name: get_site_map
tools.description: One site's structure from its sitemaps: sections, new and removed pages, what fails. Call this to see where a site is changing or breaking without crawling it. (GET /api/sites/{slug}/map)

range.description: the window for new and removed pages

section.description: a section path such as "/c" to list its pages

tools.name: list_site_events
tools.description: What changed on one site: incidents opened and resolved, code pushes, maintenance, new pages. Call this to find what changed before a number moved (clicks fell, pages got slower). (GET /api/sites/{slug}/events)

kind.description: only these kinds, comma separated (incident, resolved, push, maintenance, paused, resumed, published): kind=incident,resolved leaves pushes out

tools.name: list_failed_checks
tools.description: One site's failed checks: when, where, how, and whether each counted against uptime. Call this when uptime shows failures but no incident explains them. (GET /api/sites/{slug}/failures)

tools.name: list_incidents
tools.description: Incidents, open now or recent; open outages and slowdowns carry the likely cause. Call this to see what went wrong and why. (GET /api/incidents)

state.description: open: open now; recent: newest first, open or closed; resolved: closed ones only, newest first

kind.description: only these kinds, comma-separated: site_down,slow for outages and slowdowns

tools.name: get_incident
tools.description: One incident in full: an outage's whole diagnosis, where it was seen and how it failed. Call this for the story of one incident, open or resolved. (GET /api/incidents/{id})

tools.name: list_domains
tools.description: The team's domains: registration expiry, registrar, nameservers, status. Call this to check renewals. (GET /api/domains)

tools.name: list_public_sites
tools.description: Every public site's status and uptime, no key needed. Call this to see the public status pages' sites right now, without a key. (GET /api/public/sites)

tools.name: get_public_site
tools.description: One public site's 90 days: daily uptime, response time and outages, no key needed. Call this for a public site's history without a key. (GET /api/public/sites/{slug})

tools.name: dismiss_incident
tools.description: Dismiss an open incident as noise. Hides it from the open lists for the whole team; it never alerts again and closes without a message. Needs a Member or Admin key, on a team with 10 sites or more. (POST /api/incidents/{id}/dismiss)

tools.name: undismiss_incident
tools.description: Bring back a dismissed incident. Undoes a dismiss. Needs a Member or Admin key, on a team with 10 sites or more. (POST /api/incidents/{id}/undismiss)

tools.name: recheck_incident
tools.description: Check an incident again now. The monitor checks it again within 30 seconds, after a fix, instead of waiting for the next scheduled check. Needs a Member or Admin key, on a team with 10 sites or more. (POST /api/incidents/{id}/recheck)

tools.name: start_maintenance
tools.description: Start a maintenance window on a site now. Call this before a deploy. Needs a Member or Admin key, on a team with 10 sites or more. (POST /api/sites/{slug}/maintenance/start)

reason.description: the team's own words; never public

tools.name: end_maintenance
tools.description: End a site's maintenance windows now. Call this after a deploy. Needs a Member or Admin key, on a team with 10 sites or more. (POST /api/sites/{slug}/maintenance/end)

tools.name: remeasure_site
tools.description: Measure a site's headers and cache facts again now, after a fix. Call this after deploying a header or cache fix, instead of waiting for the daily run. Needs a Member or Admin key, on a team with 10 sites or more. (POST /api/sites/{slug}/insights/recheck)

tools.name: pause_site
tools.description: Pause a site's checks. Stops every check of the site, keeping its history, until it's resumed. Needs an Admin key, on a team with 10 sites or more. (POST /api/sites/{slug}/pause)

tools.name: resume_site
tools.description: Resume a paused site's checks. Starts the site's checks again within a minute. Needs an Admin key, on a team with 10 sites or more. (POST /api/sites/{slug}/resume)

tools.name: list_journeys
tools.description: A site's agent journeys: what each asks an agent to do, its model and schedule, and its latest verdict. Call this to see how agents fare on the site. (GET /api/sites/{slug}/journeys)

tools.name: list_journey_runs
tools.description: A journey's runs, newest first: verdicts, where they got stuck, costs and outcome checks. Call this to see how a journey has gone lately (the last 90 days) on one of its models, and to pick a run to read step by step. (GET /api/sites/{slug}/journeys/{journey}/runs)

journey.description: the journey's slug, as in its page's address /sites/{slug}/journeys/{journey}

model.description: which model's runs (one of the journey's `models`); its first model when left out

tools.name: get_journey_run
tools.description: One journey run, step by step: what the agent thought, fetched, got back and why it stopped. Call this to see exactly what an agent met on the site. (GET /api/sites/{slug}/journeys/{journey}/runs/{id})

journey.description: the journey's slug, as in its page's address /sites/{slug}/journeys/{journey}

tools.name: quote_journey
tools.description: What the journey's next run would charge, on each of its models, and what's left to spend. Call this before running a journey now, or to tell your person what one costs. (GET /api/sites/{slug}/journeys/{journey}/quote)

journey.description: the journey's slug, as in its page's address /sites/{slug}/journeys/{journey}

tools.name: run_journey
tools.description: Run a journey now, as a job. Queues a run on each of the journey's models, as Run now does. Needs an Admin key, on a team with 10 sites or more. (POST /api/sites/{slug}/journeys/{journey}/run)

journey.description: the journey's slug, as in its page's address /sites/{slug}/journeys/{journey}

tools.name: get_journey_request
tools.description: A journey run asked for with Run now: queued, running or finished, and its verdict. Poll this after asking for a run (every few seconds, as Retry-After says). (GET /api/sites/{slug}/journeys/{journey}/requests/{id})

journey.description: the journey's slug, as in its page's address /sites/{slug}/journeys/{journey}

id.description: the request's id, from the run's 202

tools.name: get_usage
tools.description: This month's journey charges: by journey and model, against the team's monthly budget. Call this to see what the team's journeys have been charged this calendar month (UTC), and how much of its budget is left. (GET /api/usage)
